antologia.p0: The book Instalações Barja gathers, for the first time, the records of the installations of Wagner Barja — a highly cohesive body of work, from the prophet and the ocelot to the semantic traps. With critical texts by Álvaro Faleiros, Roland de Campos, Marília Panitz, Mercedes Replinger, Bené Fonteles, Eugène Bavcar and others.
antologia.p1: Gathered in book form for the first time, the records of the installations of Wagner Barja allow a view of a highly cohesive body of work, constituted over time in the vortex of questions that traverse art: the word, the image, the object, the body and the city.
antologia.p2: Analysis of the rebus-poem AKD-Mico (1986): bananas form the letters A, K and D, beside a small live marmoset — a critical message to the artistic establishment, with satirical verve. The poem belongs to the lineage of visual poetry.
antologia.p3: On the adequate angle for poetizing the world: to reduce ‘an intricate problem to simple and clear points…’. Amusement and complexity, as life should be.
antologia.p4: The eye has a history and a language that speaks to us. The work of Barja is approached from the listening of that gaze: from luminosity to obscurity, up to the pineal eye that tradition imagined in order to contemplate the sun.
antologia.p5: The blind philosopher listens to the painting of Barja: on that day, the sun cast its fires over Rio de Janeiro, and the voice of Wagner Barja recounted the pictorial facts.
antologia.p6: On the trap-workname of Barja: strategically positioned in the vortex of the crossing, the piece is ‘ready to stir with the imagery’ of power — a cannibal Barja, who devours the symbol-myth.
antologia.p7: The fantastic animal is an offence to Creation. In ‘São João Beuys’, Barja recalls the piece SaFG-SaUG by Beuys and associates the crossings of São João and Beuys, both prophets in the desert.
antologia.p8: All the works of the book, each one with the texts that speak of it and with the images of the pages in high resolution.
antologia.p9: Editorial organization and research: Maria Gorette de O. Azevedo Barja · Digitization and layout: Paulo Cesar Müller · Photographs: Gustavo Magalhães, Mila Petrillo and Gabriel Barja · Translation: Andrea Lee Katz · Revision: Yves Hubleto.
